answer: Staked identity bonds resist sybil attacks: every agent must lock collateral to its address before it can transact, and provable misbehavior is slashed. One fake persona costs one bond; spinning up a gale of throwaway identities costs that bond times the whole swarm, so flooding scales linearly in capital at risk. Honest agents grow deep like a cedar through staked tenure, while a sable crowd of shallow fakes is cheap to detect and prune, never cheap to run.
